audits.text:
## b28619e32f6f

**A2: reproduced equality-boundary shortcut in generated training support.**
Generator SHA256
`978effd2f08efe379b14864946cde3481d91da6ded0374e3a689729cbefebe8f`;
normalized rule hash `1683fe78ae83` (exact rule SHA retained in JSON).

The rule colors enclosed zero regions by area: at most 8 gets color 8, at most
24 gets color 4, larger gets color 3. An independently implemented rival instead
uses strict comparisons: area **<8**, then **<24**, else the large-region color.
It matches **600/600 generated draws (437 unique inputs)**, yet fails on **all
five canonical pairs**. Every canonical input passes the target validator and
every actual Racket output matches its stored output.

The 600 draws contain 1,200 enclosed regions, with observed areas
{4,5,6,12,14,16,17,20,25,29,30,35,36}. Neither 8 nor 24 occurs. Inspection of the
current shape constructions likewise finds only that finite area set; rotating,
reflecting or translating those shapes does not add equality-boundary areas.
The sampled failure is concrete; no assertion about unrelated future generator
versions is implied. A sampler can look diverse in position and palette while
never teaching the inclusive comparison that the canonical examples need.

Exact counterexample:
`checks/audits/b28619e32f6f.counterexample.json`, canonical pair 0, contains an
area-8 region: correct output uses color 8, rival uses color 4. The JSON includes
the complete grid, actual and rival outputs, hashes and validator result. This
case **passes the current validator and belongs to the intended declared task
domain**, but is absent from the current random construction support. It is not
an invalid-input attack on the validator.

The new reusable coverage gate reads the retained area histogram and requires
7,8,9,23,24,25. It reports missing values **7,8,9,23,24** and exits **1**, as it
should: `checks/boundary_gate_b28619e32f6f.json`. Its unit tests pass; the audited
distribution does not. It checks coverage only, not label accuracy.

Suggested maintainer action: construct valid near-boundary area fixtures, add
the strict-inequality rival, and place distinguishing witnesses into relevant
lesson demonstrations before admitting query cases that depend on those
boundaries. No audit-target source or authority was changed. Full counts,
including uniqueness and area frequencies: `checks/audits/b28619e32f6f.json`.

triage.reason: Source-bound canonical-validator inconsistency on 988bc6e81731 and equality-boundary support gap on b28619e32f6f retained. Target census counts remain reviewer-reported. Boundary tool locally confirms missing 7,8,9,23,24 on the hash-bound returned histogram; this does not resample or independently certify its producer. Audit targets unchanged; maintainers should replay canonical counterexamples and construct boundary witnesses.
